selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the passage say will be discussed here instead of giving a full explanation of the whole truth?
questions.answer: It says the discussion will focus on two dangerous sources of doubt that weaken a person’s certainty in faith in this time.

questions.question: In the first matter, what is said about denial when it faces evidence?
questions.answer: It is said to be very weak and of little worth.

questions.question: In that case, what makes the witnesses’ claim powerful?
questions.answer: They actually saw the sign they are reporting.

questions.question: If someone says a thing exists somewhere, what may be enough to establish that?
questions.answer: One clear indication may be enough.

questions.question: Which statement stays within human limits: “I cannot see it” or “It does not exist at all”?
questions.answer: “I cannot see it” stays within human limits.

questions.question: What does that contrast teach about the large number of those who reject belief?
questions.answer: Their numbers do not make their position strong or decisive.

questions.question: What three ideas are used to summarize belief?
questions.answer: Knowledge, affirmation, and judgement.

questions.question: Who are the trusted witnesses in matters of Divine unity and sacred truth?
questions.answer: The many truthful spiritual people who reached high levels of certainty.

questions.question: When unbelief tries to hold a false claim as if it were something positive, how is it classified?
questions.answer: It is classified as wrong knowledge or false judgement.

questions.question: How can a form of unbelief appear to be something positive?
questions.answer: It can appear positive when it wrongly accepts or asserts a false idea.

questions.question: What is the main goal of this section of the passage?
questions.answer: Its goal is to address two major causes of doubt that disturb certainty in faith.

questions.question: In the example about the new moon of Ramadan, whose statement is treated as stronger?
questions.answer: The statement of the two ordinary people who actually saw it is treated as stronger.

questions.question: What happens when multiple people affirm the same fact?
questions.answer: Their affirmations support one another and become stronger together.

questions.question: Why does negation fail to produce the same kind of consensus?
questions.answer: Because each person’s denial is based on his own separate lack of seeing or knowing.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do deniers often use as the measure of reality?
questions.answer: They use their own inner limits, understanding, and sight.

questions.question: What is the short conclusion about negation?
questions.answer: It is split into many separate claims because each one depends on the denier’s own viewpoint.

questions.question: Why is this principle important for questions of faith?
questions.answer: Because spiritual truths should be judged by those who know and experience such matters, not by those cut off from them.

questions.question: What is the main point of the second matter?
questions.answer: People who are outside a branch of knowledge cannot give final judgement in it.

questions.question: Why is their agreement especially powerful?
questions.answer: Because many of them reached profound levels of insight and all support the truths of faith.

questions.question: Why is that easier form described as absolute ignorance?
questions.answer: Because it does not even rise to the level of making a real judgement.

questions.question: Why does the passage not fully re-explain the truth it mentions at the beginning?
questions.answer: Because it says that truth has already been firmly established elsewhere, so this section only deals with two faith-shaking doubts.

questions.question: What central rule is taught in the first part about denial and proof?
questions.answer: A denial is weak when clear proof is present.

questions.question: When people merely deny something, how do they relate to each other?
questions.answer: Each one stays separate, because one person’s denial does not really strengthen another’s.

questions.question: What is enough to establish that a thing exists?
questions.answer: Even one clear indication can establish it.
